title: Work on the Hearts and Minds of Others
hook: Derek stops reciting vaccine facts when a mother names the fear under them.
counterintuition: Power often hides in the setup, not the speech. Here the better choice is to shape hearts and minds before the visible contest begins.
tryThisNow: Before the next relevant conversation, write the one pressure word in play: hearts and minds. Then choose the smallest visible action that changes it.
keyTakeaway: Win cooperation by touching what people feel and value before you demand compliance.

breakdown.fastRead:
Anna rolls the call sheet in the soundstage. The work choice looks small, yet it can shift mirror.

Stage feels fast for Anna. It also gives the room a clean target.

Keep hearts close and plain. One clear act should change what others can do next.

If the call sheet move feels false or cruel, narrow it. Power lasts when Anna leaves fewer loose ends.
breakdown.deepRead: Dominic faces the same pattern in manager learning what each technician is proud of before changing shifts. The useful distinction is hearts and minds, buy-in, emotional investment. Apply the move through the setup, not through a generic speech.
breakdown.fullRead: Douglas sees the limit clearly in teacher persuading a resistant class by naming their real worry. The move helps only when it stays narrower than being vaguely nice to everyone. If it becomes a pose, it loses the practical force that made it useful.

examples.scenario: On the break room table, a headset waits while director Elliot locks the desk edge. Elliot must choose. The work test is whether the headset speaks now or stays mute. examples.whatToDo: Earn trust where the damage lives. Elliot should let local grief and practical needs shape the public ask.
examples.whyItMatters: Buy-in grows from contact with lived stakes. A flood plan sounds different after the mayor has sat at the table.

examples.scenario: Behind the clinic desk, nurse Francis sets down a note as the work note sits in view. Francis faces a choice. The note can reset work, or it can sit unused through hearts. implementationPlan.coreSkill: Practice reading hearts and minds before you act. The skill is to make win cooperation by touching what people feel and value before you demand compliance in a visible, bounded way instead of drifting into being vaguely nice to everyone.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a work decision exposes hearts and minds, then change the first visible artifact or sequence before making the argument.
If the other side can resist the obvious claim, then make buy-in visible through the setup first.
If the move could become being vaguely nice to everyone, then narrow it to one concrete action and one clear limit.
If people are watching for status, risk, or advantage, then decide what the room should see first and what should remain quiet.
